issue.mint_text: Korea Minting and Security Printing Corporation, Daejeon (no mint mark)

new.story: A South Korean 10 won from 2001, struck in brass. The Dabotap pagoda of Bulguksa temple stands on one side, a stone pagoda from the 700s and one of Korea's national treasures, with the value in Hangul beside it. The other side carries a big 10, the year, and the Bank of Korea's name. This brass design ran from 1983 to 2006, when a smaller, cheaper copper-colored version took its place; the collection already holds that successor.
new.notes: Both sides photographed. The value side reads 2001 over a big 10, with the Bank of Korea's name in Hangul along the bottom rim; the pagoda side shows the Dabotap pagoda with the denomination in Hangul on both sides of it. The brass color matches this 1983-2006 type, distinct from the smaller copper-plated aluminium 10 won struck from 2006. The bold value digits match the thicker-digit variant the catalogs list for 2001.
